Data, layer selection, and interpretation

Matched cohort. These are the two main-figure panels: Qwen3-8B, fixed gold N = 10, strict numeric indexed traces. There are 30 paired complete trajectories (20 discovery, 10 confirmation), with k = 1,…,10 states each. Sample IDs are remapped consistently across both modes and all layers. This selected cohort does not represent all generated outputs. Trace-format selection and the secondary split followed exploration; this is not a fresh confirmation cohort.

Secondary split. The cohort retains all 11 original discovery seeds. Of 19 original confirmation seeds, 10 are hash-selected as secondary confirmation; the other 9 join discovery. “Confirmation” throughout this viewer refers to that frozen secondary split.

Paper layers. Each mode independently maximizes discovery grouped-out-of-fold nearest-centroid (NCC) balanced accuracy; ties use discovery logistic balanced accuracy, then the earlier layer. This gives L13 and L31, whose confirmation NCC is 46% and 98%. The report’s non-thinking default L15 uses a different selection score. Selecting other layers here is exploratory; it does not redefine the paper’s selection procedure.

Projection versus readout. Each mode and layer has its own discovery-fitted PCA basis. The display uses three components; the saved confirmation NCC uses a 16-component readout, with 10% chance accuracy. Switching the displayed split changes points and their displayed centroids, but does not retrain PCA or NCC. The connecting line joins class means in k order and is not an individual observed trajectory.

Camera and scale. The paper preset retains the paper’s yaw −0.72 rad, pitch −0.45 rad, mild perspective, and uniform 0.75 non-thinking display factor. Clouds are centered and uniformly fitted separately into their panels. Axis triads are orientation cues, not magnitude scales. Absolute cloud sizes across layers or modes are not comparable here. Orthographic mode removes perspective and the 0.75 display factor. Hover and CSV export report the original coordinates.

Across-layer comparison. PCA signs and bases can change between layers and modes; synchronized cameras do not create a common PCA basis. Rotating a cloud does not alter its NCC. Use the full layer curves to inspect how sensitive the result is to layer choice.

Self-contained · No external scripts, fonts, analytics, or data requests
